claim: ISH for electroreceptor-specific Kcnab3 followed by immunostaining for Sox2 showed that the ectopic organs were indeed neuromasts (n=5/6).
source: We therefore took six of the nine larvae that had been subjected to ISH for electroreceptor-specific Kcnab3 and immunostained them for the supporting cell marker Sox2, which labels neuromasts more strongly than ampullary organs (also see Minařík et al., 2024a). This enabled direct comparison of the same larvae with and without visible neuromasts and showed that the ectopic organs were indeed neuromasts (Figure 6M-N1; n=5/6 as in one larva it was not clear whether an ectopic offshoot was indeed present).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6M-N1.

claim: Ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line were seen in a majority of larvae (n=10/14; 71%) in which Bmp signalling had been blocked for 20 hr from stage 36.
source: Overall, therefore, ectopic offshoots of the supraorbital neuromast line (compare Figure 6M1,N1 with wildtype Sox2 expression at stage 45 in Figure 2—figure supplement 1K and L) were seen in a majority of larvae (n=10/14; 71%) in which Bmp signalling had been blocked for 20 hr from stage 36, where this could be determined (n=5/8 after ISH for Cacna1d; n=5/6 after ISH for Kcnab3 followed by immunostaining for Sox2).
evidence: This is a summary of the data on ectopic neuromast offshoots.

claim: At stage 36, neuromast primordia are already forming in the supraorbital primordium.
source: At stage 36, neuromast primordia are already forming in the supraorbital primordium (as shown by Sox2 expression; Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: At stages 36–38, immunoreactivity for pSMAD1/5/9 suggests that Bmp signalling is most prominent in lateral line nerves, rather than the supraorbital lateral line primordium.
source: At stages 36–38, immunoreactivity for pSMAD1/5/9 suggests that Bmp signalling is most prominent in this region in lateral line nerves, rather than the supraorbital lateral line primordium (Figure 2E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2E-H.

claim: The Bmp signalling activity during stages 36–38 that is required to prevent ectopic secondary neuromast formation from the supraorbital neuromast line might be active in lateral line nerves, rather than the lateral line primordium itself.
source: This suggests the intriguing hypothesis that the Bmp signalling activity during stages 36–38 (the approximate period of DMH1 treatment) that is required to prevent ectopic secondary neuromast formation from the supraorbital neuromast line, might be active in lateral line nerves, rather than the lateral line primordium itself.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the immunohistochemistry data and the DMH1 treatment results.

claim: DMH1-treated larvae had significantly more ampullary organs overall than DMSO controls (p<0.0001).
source: Statistical analysis using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney (Wilcoxon rank sum) test confirmed that DMH1-treated larvae had significantly more ampullary organs overall than DMSO controls (p<0.0001; Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 7A and Supplementary file 3.

claim: All individual ampullary organ fields had significantly more ampullary organs in DMH1-treated larvae than in DMSO controls.
source: This was also the case for each individual ampullary organ field (Figure 7B; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 7B and Supplementary file 3.

claim: DMH1-treated larvae (n=17) had significantly more ampullary organs than older (2.0/2.8 cm) wild-type larvae (n=10), both overall (p<0.0001) and in all fields except the ventral supraorbital and posterior preopercular fields.
source: Furthermore, the DMH1-treated larvae (n=17) had significantly more ampullary organs than older (2.0/2.8 cm) wild-type larvae (n=10), both overall (p<0.0001; Figure 8A) and in all fields except the ventral supraorbital and posterior preopercular fields (Figure 8B; Supplementary file 3; the same colour-coded schematic is shown in Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data shown in Figure 8A and B and Supplementary file 3.

claim: There was no significant difference between ampullary organ numbers in 2.0 cm versus 2.8 cm wild-type larvae, either overall (p=0.4206) or in any individual field (p>0.05 for each field).
source: (Note: the five 2.0 cm and five 2.8 cm wild-type larvae were grouped together for statistical comparison with DMH1-treated larvae because using a two-tailed Mann-Whitney test showed that there was no significant difference between ampullary organ numbers in 2.0 cm versus 2.8 cm larvae, either overall [p=0.4206] or in any individual field [p>0.05 for each field].)
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of counting data in Supplementary file 3.

claim: Blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36, before the first ampullary organ primordia form, results in supernumerary ampullary organs in all fields.
source: Overall, these results show that blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36, before the first ampullary organ primordia form, results in supernumerary ampullary organs in all fields.
evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claim: Blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36 results in ectopic ampullary organs forming in the dorsalmost fields.
source: Furthermore, ectopic ampullary organs form in the dorsalmost fields, and an ectopic offshoot of the supraorbital neuromast line develops in a majority of larvae.
evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claim: Blocking Bmp signalling for 20 hr from stage 36 results in an ectopic offshoot of the supraorbital neuromast line developing in a majority of larvae.
source: Furthermore, ectopic ampullary organs form in the dorsalmost fields, and an ectopic offshoot of the supraorbital neuromast line develops in a majority of larvae.
evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claim: During normal development, Bmp signalling dampens ampullary organ formation, preventing the over-production of ampullary organs in each individual field and the formation of ectopic ampullary organs in the most dorsal fields.
source: This suggests that during normal development, Bmp signalling dampens ampullary organ formation, preventing the over-production of ampullary organs in each individual field and the formation of ectopic ampullary organs in the most dorsal fields.
evidence: This is an inference based on the DMH1 treatment data.

claim: Bmp5 proved to be expressed in ampullary organ primordia (though not neuromast primordia), as well as in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts in sterlet.
source: In this study, we identified opposing roles for Bmp signalling in ampullary organ development in sterlet. We began by investigating Bmp5, the only Bmp ligand gene in our late-larval paddlefish lateral line organ-enriched gene-set (Modrell et al., 2017a). In sterlet, Bmp5 proved to be expressed in ampullary organ primordia (though not neuromast primordia), as well as in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts.
evidence: This is a summary of the Bmp5 expression data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Significantly fewer ampullary organs formed when Bmp5 was targeted for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos.
source: Significantly fewer ampullary organs formed when Bmp5 was targeted for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos, suggesting that during normal development, Bmp5 promotes ampullary organ formation.
evidence: This is a summary of the CRISPR/Cas9 data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Blocking Bmp signalling globally at stages just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development led to significantly more ampullary organs forming in all fields.
source: In contrast, blocking Bmp signalling globally at stages just prior to the onset of ampullary organ development led to significantly more ampullary organs forming in all fields.
evidence: This is a summary of the DMH1 treatment data shown in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claim: Bmp signalling activity is required to prevent too many ampullary organs from developing.
source: Hence, Bmp signalling activity is required to prevent too many ampullary organs from developing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the DMH1 treatment data.

claim: The precise function and timing of action of Bmp5 in promoting ampullary organ formation remain to be determined.
source: The early expression of Bmp5 in ampullary organ primordia, but not neuromast primordia, suggested a role specifically in ampullary organ development. Indeed, targeting Bmp5 for CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis in G0-injected sterlet embryos led to significantly fewer ampullary organs forming, with no effect on neuromast formation. Its precise function and timing of action in promoting ampullary organ formation remain to be determined.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study and future directions.

claim: It could be informative to test whether inhibiting Bmp signalling using DMH1 for discrete periods at successively later time-points recapitulates the Bmp5 crispant phenotype.
source: Although beyond the scope of this study, it could be informative to test whether inhibiting Bmp signalling using DMH1 for discrete periods at successively later time-points recapitulates the Bmp5 crispant phenotype.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future experiments.

claim: It would be interesting to see whether developing ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants show any changes in the expression of the Bmp/Wnt inhibitor genes Sostdc1 and/or Apcdd1.
source: Similarly, it would be interesting to see whether developing ampullary organs in Bmp5 crispants show any changes in the expression of the Bmp/Wnt inhibitor genes Sostdc1 and/or Apcdd1.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future experiments.

claim: In zebrafish, Bmp5 expression has been reported in the migrating posterior lateral line primordium.
source: In zebrafish, Bmp5 expression has been reported in the migrating posterior lateral line primordium (Thisse and Thisse, 2004), which also expresses Bmp4b and Bmp2a (Mowbray et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: The migrating posterior lateral line primordium in zebrafish also expresses Bmp4b and Bmp2a.
source: In zebrafish, Bmp5 expression has been reported in the migrating posterior lateral line primordium (Thisse and Thisse, 2004), which also expresses Bmp4b and Bmp2a (Mowbray et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: A role for Bmp signalling in neuromast development has not been identified in zebrafish.
source: However, a role for Bmp signalling in neuromast development has not been identified (see, for example, Piotrowski and Baker, 2014; Chitnis, 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Small-molecule inhibition of Bmp signalling from late epiboly or neural plate stages led to expansion of the posterior (but not pre-otic) lateral line placode in zebrafish.
source: Small-molecule inhibition of Bmp signalling from late epiboly or neural plate stages led to expansion of the posterior (but not pre-otic) lateral line placode, suggesting that a much earlier phase of Bmp signalling restricts the posterior lateral line placode from expanding both posteriorly and laterally (Nikaido et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: A much earlier phase of Bmp signalling restricts the posterior lateral line placode from expanding both posteriorly and laterally in zebrafish.
source: Small-molecule inhibition of Bmp signalling from late epiboly or neural plate stages led to expansion of the posterior (but not pre-otic) lateral line placode, suggesting that a much earlier phase of Bmp signalling restricts the posterior lateral line placode from expanding both posteriorly and laterally (Nikaido et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the results of small-molecule inhibition experiments, supported by a citation.

claim: In mature neuromasts in zebrafish (at 5 dpf), scRNA-seq data show that Bmp5 is expressed in neuromast hair cell progenitor populations and downregulated as hair cells differentiate.
source: In mature neuromasts in zebrafish (at 5 dpf), scRNA-seq data show that Bmp5 is expressed in neuromast hair cell progenitor populations and downregulated as hair cells differentiate (Lush et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Bmp5 is among the genes upregulated in 5-dpf zebrafish neuromasts within one hour after neomycin-induced hair cell death.
source: Furthermore, Bmp5 is among the genes upregulated in 5-dpf zebrafish neuromasts within one hour after neomycin-induced hair cell death (Jiang et al., 2014; Heller et al., 2022), and in the postnatal mouse cochlea after gentamycin-induced hair cell death (Bai et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Bmp5 is among the genes upregulated in the postnatal mouse cochlea after gentamycin-induced hair cell death.
source: Furthermore, Bmp5 is among the genes upregulated in 5-dpf zebrafish neuromasts within one hour after neomycin-induced hair cell death (Jiang et al., 2014; Heller et al., 2022), and in the postnatal mouse cochlea after gentamycin-induced hair cell death (Bai et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Bmp5 may be important for hair cell regeneration.
source: Hence, Bmp5 may be important for hair cell regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data from zebrafish and mouse.

claim: Neomycin treatment at late-larval stages (stages 44/45) in the Siberian sturgeon (A. baerii) kills electroreceptors, as well as hair cells, both of which subsequently regenerate.
source: Neomycin treatment at late-larval stages (stages 44/45) in the Siberian sturgeon (A. baerii) kills electroreceptors, as well as hair cells, both of which subsequently regenerate (Fan et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Given the expression of Bmp5 in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts in sterlet, Bmp5 could play a role in the homeostasis (and regeneration after injury) of electroreceptors as well as hair cells.
source: Given the expression of Bmp5 in mature ampullary organs and neuromasts in sterlet, Bmp5 could play a role in the homeostasis (and regeneration after injury) of electroreceptors as well as hair cells.
evidence: This is speculation based on the Bmp5 expression data in sterlet and the known role of Bmp5 in hair cell regeneration in other species.

claim: Diffuse, more transient Bmp4 expression was identified between stages 40–42 within developing ampullary organ fields and neuromast regions in sterlet.
source: In addition to Bmp5 expression in developing ampullary organ primordia (but not neuromast primordia) and mature ampullary organs and neuromasts, we also identified diffuse, more transient Bmp4 expression between stages 40–42 within developing ampullary organ fields and neuromast regions.
evidence: This is a summary of the Bmp4 expression data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Persistent Bmp4 expression was seen in the migrating lateral line primordia on the trunk in sterlet.
source: Persistent expression was also seen in the migrating lateral line primordia on the trunk, consistent with a report of Bmp4b (as well as Bmp2a) expression in the migrating posterior lateral line primordium (primI) in zebrafish (Mowbray et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a summary of the Bmp4 expression data shown in Figure 3, supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Additional unidentified Bmp ligand(s) are likely to be expressed in sterlet, as pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity was seen throughout lateral line development.
source: Additional unidentified Bmp ligand(s) are also likely to be expressed in sterlet, as pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity (a proxy for Bmp signalling pathway activity; Schmierer and Hill, 2007) was seen throughout lateral line development, including within elongating lateral line primordia and afferent lateral line nerves (which extend together with all lateral line primordia as they elongate or migrate; Winklbauer, 1989; Northcutt, 2005; Piotrowski and Baker, 2014), as well as at the periphery of developing ampullary organs and neuromasts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pSMAD1/5/9 immunoreactivity data shown in Figure 2.

claim: DMH1 blocks signalling through the type I receptors Acvr1 (Alk2), Acvrl1 (Alk1), and Bmpr1a (Alk3).
source: We identified a role for Bmp signalling in preventing too many ampullary organs from forming, using the selective Bmp pathway inhibitor DMH1 (Hao et al., 2010). DMH1 blocks signalling through the type I receptors Acvr1 (Alk2), Acvrl1 (Alk1), and Bmpr1a (Alk3) (Hao et al., 2010; Cross et al., 2011), all of which signal via Smad1/5/9 (Yadin et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Acvr1 (Alk2), Acvrl1 (Alk1), and Bmpr1a (Alk3) all signal via Smad1/5/9.
source: We identified a role for Bmp signalling in preventing too many ampullary organs from forming, using the selective Bmp pathway inhibitor DMH1 (Hao et al., 2010). DMH1 blocks signalling through the type I receptors Acvr1 (Alk2), Acvrl1 (Alk1), and Bmpr1a (Alk3) (Hao et al., 2010; Cross et al., 2011), all of which signal via Smad1/5/9 (Yadin et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Acvr1 (Alk2) binds Bmp5/6/7/8.
source: Acvr1 (Alk2) binds Bmp5/6/7/8; Acvrl1 (Alk1) binds Bmp9/10, and Bmpr1a (Alk3) binds Bmp2/4/5/6/7/8 and Gdf5/6/7 (also known as Bmp14/13/12) (Yadin et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Acvrl1 (Alk1) binds Bmp9/10.
source: Acvr1 (Alk2) binds Bmp5/6/7/8; Acvrl1 (Alk1) binds Bmp9/10, and Bmpr1a (Alk3) binds Bmp2/4/5/6/7/8 and Gdf5/6/7 (also known as Bmp14/13/12) (Yadin et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Bmpr1a (Alk3) binds Bmp2/4/5/6/7/8 and Gdf5/6/7 (also known as Bmp14/13/12).
source: Acvr1 (Alk2) binds Bmp5/6/7/8; Acvrl1 (Alk1) binds Bmp9/10, and Bmpr1a (Alk3) binds Bmp2/4/5/6/7/8 and Gdf5/6/7 (also known as Bmp14/13/12) (Yadin et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Although a role for Bmp signalling has not been identified in neuromast formation, this pathway is important for the formation of inner-ear sensory patches, within which hair cells also differentiate.
source: Although a role for Bmp signalling has not been identified in neuromast formation (see, for example, Piotrowski and Baker, 2014; Chitnis, 2021), this pathway is important for the formation of inner-ear sensory patches, within which hair cells also differentiate.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles and draws on established knowledge.

claim: Bmp4 is an early marker for all sensory patches in the chicken inner ear, and for the cristae (vestibular sensory patches of the semicircular canals) in mouse.
source: Bmp4 is an early marker for all sensory patches in the chicken inner ear, and for the cristae (vestibular sensory patches of the semicircular canals) in mouse (Wu and Oh, 1996; Morsli et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Conditional knockout experiments showed that Bmp4 is required for the formation of the cristae in mouse.
